newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees '97 peso devaluation of 13 to 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees '97 peso devaluation of 13 to 15 pct.

text.p: Colombia's central bank forecast Thursday a devaluation of between 13 and 15 percent in the value of the peso against the dollar in 1997.
The forecast is based on an estimated rate of inflation of between 16 and 18 percent, Roberto Junguito, the bank's co- director said.
He also said Colombia would accumulate $1 billion in foreign reserves in 1997.

At the same event, the National Agrarian Congress, President Ernesto Samper said he would increase public spending by 21 percent in nominal terms in 1997 -- about 10 percent lower than in previous years.
Colombia's central bank is scheduled to issue firm goals for inflation, devaluation, balance of payments and other key macroeconomic figures after a meeting Friday.
The target for peso devaluation was 13.5 percent in nominal terms for 1996. In practice, the peso has sunk less than three percent so far this year in the face of a sliding dollar.
"The central bank will agree Friday to fiscal adjustment with less strict exchange rate and monetary policies for 1997," Junguito told congress delegates.
